chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Earl Hines, Don Redman and female orchestra leaders
summary: Hughes asks about local big names; she recalls a woman leader with a five-piece group and the north side.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. And there were even some local big names, I mean Earl Hines -- even Don Dedman.
I didn't know that Don Dedman --
He had a group. Well, he wasn't from there. He evidently worked there for
a time. Presumably before he went to New York in 1923. He had a group called the Broadway Syncopaters.

The name rings a bell but I don't suppose I was getting out at the time. We had two local groups, one band, -- I'd say about nine pieces under the direction of Shadine Walker, a female conductor and there was a small combination, Gertrude Long who had a band and they played all the local dances and clubs.
You mentioned another female orchestra leader besides Shadine Walker.
Okay, you just said that one. I'm sorry.

She had a small com -- she always carried a small group of five pieces -- piano -- she played piano and bass, that is, she carried bass, drums and a couple horns, I guess. I don't remember some of the musicians that she had. But there would be different ones at different times. But she was one of the local leaders and she had a very good band, some of the best Swing musicians

around at that time. Then there was the north side from which Billy Eckst[e]in and Roy Eldridge are from. There's a lot of good musicians from that part of town -- sort of north of Pittsburgh, across the Allegheny River and they played in downtown Pittsburgh. And these would be the musicians that I would run into at the Crawford Grill upn Wylie Avenue.

Although I went to affairs quite frequently and I heard a lot of music. I wasn't part of the scene, you know, I was just an observer more or less. I mean, I wasn't known downtown Pittsburgh as one of the local entertainers. It took me a little while to establish myself. I knew the musicians and the musicians knew me, but I wasn't part of the scene. I wasn't a working performer.
